comparator.name: Bachelor Sustainable Innovation
comparator.academicYear: 2026-2027 current programme and course records; official 180-EC curriculum reconstruction checked 2026-10-05
comparator.sourceNotes: The current TU/e programme and degree-structure material presents Sustainable Innovation as a 180-EC bachelor combining technical, economic and social-science analysis of sustainability transitions. The official curriculum table accounts for three 60-EC years and identifies the core in sustainable technology in society, industrial ecology, economics and policy, research methods, modelling, integration projects, specialisation-linked technical courses, elective/Impact of Technology space and a 10-EC final project. Current 2026-2027 TU/e course records confirm that the named Sustainable Innovation, statistics and integration courses remain active. The generic target does not select between the two programme specialisations; Sustainable Energy is selected by the neutral official-order tie-break and its technical options are instantiated without reference to UCR fit.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest programme combines sustainability transitions with economics, policy, governance, business, behavioural analysis, research and environmental evidence. A second coherent route follows the official Sustainable Energy direction and materially increases climate, energy-system, Earth-system, quantitative and environmental-design study. The remaining urban-planning and mobility direction cannot support a distinct 24-course programme from courses available to the fixed cohort.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Sustainability Essentials I establishes environmental, social and economic dimensions of sustainable development.
Sustainability Essentials II develops systems thinking around socio-technical sustainability challenges.
Climate Change uses physical science to explain a central sustainability problem, while TU/e supplies a broader technology-physics foundation.
Life Cycle Analysis & Circular Economy directly addresses material flows, environmental impacts and circular strategies.
Renewable System Design addresses energy-system performance and design; TU/e provides dedicated thermodynamics.
Earth System Science Tools provides quantitative modelling for environmental systems.
Living with Water addresses environmental flows and infrastructure, but not TU/e's full heat-and-flow engineering course.
UCR has renewable-system design but no combustion-engine design project.
UCR has applied environmental projects but no equivalent specialisation-specific engineering design project.
Introduction to Economics supplies market and firm foundations for innovation analysis.
International Macroeconomics addresses growth, policy and economic change; TU/e frames the advanced course specifically around innovation.
Public Economics directly examines externalities, market failure and policy intervention.
Econometrics supports empirical policy evaluation, while TU/e teaches dedicated social cost-benefit analysis.
Comparative Politics provides institutional analysis within the societal component.
Governance of Sustainability directly addresses advanced institutional and collective governance of transitions.
Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations uses design thinking and business-model development; it is not an engineering-design substitute.
Strategy & Digital Transformation examines organisational strategy and technology adoption.
UCR distributes applied innovation work across courses but has no equivalent named managing-sustainable-technology project.
Research Methods & Statistics covers research design, surveys, experiments and inference.
Qualitative Research Methodology develops advanced interviewing, observation and interpretive research.
Mathematical Methods includes calculus and quantitative modelling.
Research in a Sustainable Delta provides applied integrative sustainability research.
TU/e preserves 10 EC of first-year elective space; the UCR pathways are complete fixed examples.
TU/e preserves 20 EC of second-year elective and Impact of Technology space.
TU/e preserves 10 EC of third-year elective and Impact of Technology space.
TU/e preserves 20 EC of additional third-year elective space.
TU/e requires a 10-EC Bachelor Final Project. UCR optional independent research is shown separately.

notes.text: TU/e integrates innovation sciences with dedicated technical specialisation courses, engineering and design-based projects, economic-policy analysis, elective and Impact of Technology space, and a required Bachelor Final Project. UCR can build strong sustainability-transition and renewable-energy/environmental-system programmes, but it does not reproduce TU/e's engineering sequence, specialisation-specific technical projects or compulsory final project.
